RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
In simple terms — instead of relying solely on what an LLM was trained on, RAG lets the model retrieve relevant information from an external knowledge base at query time, then generate a response grounded in that data.
Result: more accurate, up-to-date, and context-aware answers.

GPT stands for Generative Pre-trained Transformer.
In simple terms — it's a large language model (LLM) trained on vast amounts of text data that can understand and generate human-like language. ChatGPT is OpenAI's product built on top of GPT models.
It's capable of writing, reasoning, summarising, coding, and answering questions — but it's a general-purpose tool.

MCP — Model Context Protocol — is an open standard introduced by Anthropic that defines how AI models connect to external tools, data sources, and systems in a standardised way.
Think of it as a universal plug for AI — instead of custom integrations for every tool, MCP provides a common interface so LLMs can interact with databases, APIs, files, and services consistently.
It's becoming an important building block in agentic AI architectures.

Where MCP standardises how agents connect to tools and data, A2A standardises how agents talk to each other — enabling multi-agent systems to collaborate across different vendors and frameworks.
Together, MCP and A2A are shaping the interoperability layer of the agentic AI ecosystem.

NLP — Natural Language Processing — is the branch of AI that enables computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.
It powers everything from search engines and autocorrect to chatbots, sentiment analysis, and now LLMs like GPT and Claude.
Core NLP tasks: tokenisation, named entity recognition, POS tagging, text classification, sentiment analysis, machine translation, summarisation, and question answering.

NLU and NLG are two key components of conversational AI systems:
🔹 NLU (Natural Language Understanding)
Helps a machine understand what a user means — intent detection, entity extraction, context resolution. "Book a flight to Delhi tomorrow" → understands: action=book, destination=Delhi, date=tomorrow.
🔹 NLG (Natural Language Generation)
Helps a machine produce human-like responses — turning structured data or logic into natural language text.
Together, NLU + NLG form the intelligence layer of conversational systems.

Conversational AI refers to systems that enable natural, human-like dialogues between machines and people — chatbots, voice assistants, and intelligent customer service systems.
Modern conversational AI combines:
• NLU (understanding user intent)
• Dialogue management (managing conversation state)
• NLG (generating natural responses)
• LLMs (for open-ended, context-rich conversations)

An ontology in AI is a formal, structured representation of knowledge — defining concepts, categories, relationships, and rules within a specific domain.
Think of it as a vocabulary + a map of how things relate to each other. Example: in healthcare, an ontology defines that "Paracetamol is-a Drug", "Drug treats Fever", "Fever is-a Symptom".
Ontologies power knowledge graphs, semantic search, and reasoning systems — and are foundational to many enterprise AI knowledge bases.

Examples: Google's Knowledge Graph powers search results. LinkedIn's talent graph connects people, skills, and companies. Medical knowledge graphs connect symptoms, diseases, and treatments.
They're used in semantic search, recommendation systems, fraud detection, and conversational AI for grounding responses in real-world facts.

Prompt engineering is the practice of designing inputs to AI models (like GPT or Claude) to get the most accurate, useful, and consistent outputs.
Key techniques:
• Zero-shot — just describe the task directly
• Few-shot — give examples of input/output pairs
• Chain-of-thought — ask the model to reason step by step
• Role prompting — "You are an expert in..."
• Output formatting — specify JSON, bullet points, tables
It's a critical skill for anyone building GenAI applications — small changes in wording can dramatically change output quality.
